name: Asterion
summary: At Bashal'Aran, Asterion remains bound to a moonstone seal. The ancient Highborne once served governor Athrikus Narassin, and now his spirit waits among the ruins for release.

sections.title: A Servant of Ancient Splendor
sections.body: Before the Great Sundering, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara. She appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern them, and Asterion served as his right hand. Renowned for physical combat and arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among Bashal'Aran's people. He often traveled between the sister cities to see to their citizens' needs.

sections.title: The Moonstone Prison
sections.body: For reasons lost to time, Asterion fell out of favor with Athrikus Narassin. His master fashioned a powerful moonstone seal, an inescapable magical cage meant to confine him in Bashal'Aran. The centuries of confinement brought Asterion agony. Even death offered no release: his spirit remained bound to the ruined shrine after the world cracked open and demons overran the settlement.

sections.title: Vengeance from the Grave
sections.body: Vile satyrs and grells roam Bashal'Aran, feeding on its lingering arcane power, yet they shun the shrine where Asterion's ghost lingers. An Alliance adventurer can take the moonstone seal from the satyrs and shatter it in Ameth'Aran, breaking Asterion's spectral chains at last. Freedom brings no peace. With Athrikus Narassin still enduring, Asterion turns from ten thousand years of despair toward vengeance.

aliases: who is the ghost in bashal'aran
faq.answer: Asterion is an ancient Highborne ghost at the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Before the Sundering, he was an accomplished mage and the second in command to governor Athrikus Narassin.
Athrikus Narassin bound Asterion with a magical moonstone seal. The reasons for their falling out are unknown, but the powerful enchantment held Asterion's spirit for millennia, even after death.

faq.q: Why don't the satyrs in Bashal'Aran attack him?
faq.answer: Satyrs and grells feed on the lingering arcane energies in Bashal'Aran, but keep away from the shrine where Asterion is bound. The satyrs possess the moonstone seal that anchors his captivity, rather than meddling with his spirit.

faq.q: Where did Asterion live in life?
faq.answer: Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran. He often traveled south to its twin city, Ameth'Aran, to tend to civic affairs under Queen Azshara's governor.

faq.q: What happens after you free him?
faq.answer: Asterion hopes that breaking the moonstone seal will end the imprisonment that continued beyond his death. What follows is told in the hidden passage.

faq.q: Is Asterion hostile to modern night elves?
faq.answer: No. Though Asterion is an ancient Highborne from Queen Azshara's court, he is peaceful toward Alliance travelers and seeks their help to break his ancient magical bondage.

angles.text: Asterion is a tragic relic from before the Sundering. His story shows the cruel internal politics among the Highborne before Azshara invited the Burning Legion into their lands.
In life, Asterion was celebrated for his command of the arcane and his skill in physical combat. His story offers a glimpse of early Kaldorei spellcraft.
Asterion is one of the rare Highborne spirits willing to trust and aid Alliance adventurers. He seeks their help to break his prison of ten thousand years.
